paragraphs: Genesco Inc., incorporated in 1934 in the State of Tennessee, is a leading retailer and wholesaler of branded footwear, apparel and accessories with net sales for Fiscal 2026 of $2.4 billion. During Fiscal 2026, we operated four reportable business segments (not including corporate): (i) Journeys Group, comprised of the Journeys®, Journeys Kidz® and Little Burgundy® retail footwear chains and e-commerce operations; (ii) Schuh Group, comprised of the Schuh retail footwear chain and e-commerce operations; (iii) Johnston & Murphy Group, comprised of Johnston & Murphy® retail operations, e-commerce operations and wholesale distribution of products under the Johnston & Murphy® brand; and (iv) Genesco Brands Group, comprised of the licensed Dockers® ("Dockers") and Levi's® ("Levi's") brands, as well as other brands we license for footwear. We also source, design, market and distribute footwear, apparel and accessories at wholesale, primarily under our Johnston & Murphy brand, the licensed Dockers® brand, the licensed Levi's® brand and other brands that we license for footwear to over 900 retail accounts in the United States, including a number of leading department, discount, and specialty stores as well as e-commerce retailers. Our license with Levi's expires in May 2026 and we are in the process of exiting that business.

During the second quarter of Fiscal 2026, we signed a multi-year licensing agreement with Kontoor Brands, Inc. ("Kontoor") to design, source market and distribute men's, women's and children's footwear under the Wrangler® brand ("Wrangler"). We expect to launch the first Wrangler footwear collection under the licensing agreement in the Fall of calendar year 2026.

During the third quarter of Fiscal 2026, we announced the formation of the Journeys Global Retail Group which unites Journeys, Schuh and Little Burgundy. This alignment creates a powerful opportunity across our retail banners to position the business as the world's leading style-led, youth footwear retail group, with a sharp focus on the female consumer. The Journeys Global Retail Group will boost our global voice, unlock greater growth potential for brand partners and elevate our world-class talent.

At January 31, 2026, we operated 1,236 retail footwear, apparel and accessory stores located primarily throughout the United States and Puerto Rico, including 63 footwear stores in Canada and 118 footwear stores in the United Kingdom ("U.K.") and the Republic of Ireland ("ROI"). We plan to open a total of approximately 23 new retail stores and to close approximately 75 retail stores in Fiscal 2027 as part of our ongoing store optimization efforts.

Shorthand references to fiscal years (e.g., "Fiscal 2026") refer to the fiscal year ended on the Saturday nearest January 31st in the named year (e.g., January 31, 2026). Fiscal 2026 and 2025 were 52-week years and Fiscal 2024 was a 53-week year. The terms "Company," "Genesco," "we," "our" or "us" as used herein and unless otherwise stated or indicated by context refer to Genesco Inc. and its subsidiaries. All information contained in Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," which is referred to in this Item 1 of this report, is incorporated by such reference in Item 1.

Across our company, we aspire to create and curate leading footwear brands that represent style, innovation and self-expression and to be the destination for our consumers' favorite fashion footwear. Each of our businesses has a strong strategic position grounded in a deep and ever-evolving understanding of the customers it serves. We strive to build enduring relationships with our target customers, leveraging our deep consumer and market insights. We seek to excite and constantly exceed customer expectations by delivering distinctive products and experiences, using our deep direct-to-consumer expertise across physical and digital channels. The strength of our concepts and the advantages we have built over time have established long-lasting leadership positions that make our footwear businesses outstanding on their own, but what they share through the benefit of synergies makes them even stronger together. We have evolved our strategy to focus more closely around the consumer with our footwear first strategy, comprised of four strategic growth drivers: 1) create and curate winning product, 2) elevate our distinctive retail and consumer brands, 3) deliver exceptional consumer experiences, and 4) build amazing teams. We anticipate continuing to optimize our store footprint in the future, concentrating on locations that we believe will be most productive, as well as closing certain stores, but improving productivity in our existing locations and investing in store remodels, technology and infrastructure to support omni-channel retailing.

We have made acquisitions, including the acquisitions of the Schuh Group in June 2011, Little Burgundy in December 2015 and Togast in January 2020. We expect to concentrate our efforts on opportunities to leverage our direct-to-consumer capabilities to grow our branded platform and leverage its strategies at the appropriate time going forward.

More generally, we work to develop strategies to mitigate the risks we view as material, including those discussed under the caption "Forward Looking Statements," above, and those discussed in Item 1A, "Risk Factors". Among the most important of these factors are those related to consumer demand. Conditions in the economy can affect demand, resulting in changes in sales and, as prices are adjusted to drive sales and manage inventories, in gross margins. Because fashion trends influencing many of our target customers can change rapidly, we believe that our ability to react quickly to those changes has been important to our success. Even when we succeed in aligning our merchandise offerings with consumer preferences, those preferences may affect results, for example, by driving sales of products with lower average selling prices or products which are more widely available in the marketplace and thus more subject to competitive pressures than our typical offering. Moreover, economic factors, such as inflation, supply chain disruptions and increased logistics costs, and any future economic contraction, inflationary trends, and changes in tax and tariff policies, may reduce the consumer's disposable income or willingness to purchase discretionary items, and thus may reduce demand for our merchandise, regardless of our skill in detecting and responding to fashion trends. We believe our experience and discipline in merchandising and the buying power associated with our relative size and importance in the industry segments in which we compete are important factors in our ability to mitigate risks associated with changing customer preferences and other changes in consumer demand.

The Journeys Group accounted for 61% of our net sales in Fiscal 2026. Journeys stores target customers in the 13 to 22 year age group through the use of youth-oriented trends and multi-channel media. Journeys stores carry predominately branded merchandise across a wide range of prices. The Journeys Kidz stores sell footwear and accessories primarily for younger children, toddler age to 12 years old. Little Burgundy stores sell footwear and accessories to fashion-oriented men and women in the 21 to 34 year age group ranging from students to young professionals.

At January 31, 2026, Journeys Group operated 965 stores, including 741 Journeys stores, 194 Journeys Kidz stores and 30 Little Burgundy stores averaging approximately 2,100 square feet, located primarily in malls and factory outlet centers throughout the United States, Puerto Rico and Canada, selling footwear and accessories for children, teenagers and young adults. Journeys
Group's e-commerce websites include the following: journeys.com, journeyskidz.com, journeys.ca and littleburgundyshoes.com. In Fiscal 2026, the Journeys Group closed a net of 41 stores.

Consumer spending is affected by poor and/or volatile economic conditions and other factors and may significantly harm our business, affecting our financial condition, liquidity, and results of operations.
Failure to protect our reputation could have a material adverse effect on our brand names.
Our success depends on our ability to respond to changing consumer preferences, identify and interpret consumer trends, and successfully market new products.
Our failure to appropriately address emerging sustainability matters could have a material adverse impact on our reputation and, as a result, our business.
Our results may be adversely affected by declines in consumer traffic in malls.
Our results of operations are subject to seasonal and quarterly fluctuations.
Changes in the retail industry could have a material adverse effect on our business or financial condition.
Our business is intensely competitive and increased or new competition could have a material adverse effect on us.

If our online e-commerce sites, or those of our customers, do not function effectively or meet the expectations or preferences of our customers, our business and financial results could be materially adversely affected.
Investments and Infrastructure Risks
We face a number of risks in opening new stores and renewing leases on existing stores.
Any acquisitions we make or new businesses we launch, as well as any dispositions of assets or businesses, involve a degree of risk.
Goodwill recorded with acquisitions is subject to impairment which could reduce the Company's profitability.
Technology, Data Security and Privacy Risks
The operation of our business is heavily dependent on our information systems.
Our Information Technology Restructuring Initiative May Not Achieve Expected Results and Could Disrupt Our Business Operations.
We are subject to payment-related risks that could increase our operating costs, expose us to fraud or theft, subject us to potential liability and disrupt our business.
A privacy breach, through a cybersecurity incident or otherwise, or failure to comply with privacy laws could materially adversely affect our business.
Data protection requirements are constantly evolving and these requirements could adversely affect our business and operating results.

The utilization, expansion and management of machine learning and other types of artificial intelligence in our business could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Operational, Supply Chain and Third-Party Risks
Increased operating costs, including wage increases resulting from potential increases in the minimum wage or competitive pressures, could have an adverse effect on our results.
If we lose key members of management or are unable to attract and retain the talent required for our business, our operating results could suffer.
The loss of, or disruption in, one of our distribution centers and other factors affecting the distribution of merchandise, including freight cost, could materially adversely affect our business.
An increase in the cost or a disruption in the flow of our imported products could adversely affect our business.
We are dependent on third-party vendors and licensors for the merchandise we sell.
Tax, Legal, Regulatory, Global and Other External Risks
Changes in tax laws may result in increased volatility in our effective tax rates.
Establishing and protecting our intellectual property is critical to our business.
The scope of our non-U.S. operations exposes our performance to risks including foreign, political, legal and economic conditions and exchange rate fluctuations.
paragraphs: Our business is subject to a variety of risks which might have a material impact on our business. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below and the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes to those statements. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties that we do not presently know about or that we currently consider immaterial may also affect our business operations and financial performance. If any of the events described below occur, our business, financial condition, cash flows or results of operations could be adversely affected in a material way. This could cause the trading price of our stock to decline, perhaps significantly, and you may lose part or all of your investment.

The success of our business depends to a significant extent upon the level of consumer spending in general and on our product categories. A number of factors may affect the level of consumer spending on merchandise that we offer, including, among other things:
• general economic and industry conditions, including the risks associated with recessions or other macroeconomic conditions and pressures such as inflationary impacts and supply chain challenges;
• weather conditions; • energy costs, which affect gasoline and home heating prices; • the level of consumer debt;
• pricing of products, including the impact of the imposition of tariffs; • interest rates;
• public health issues (including pandemics and quarantines); • tax rates, refunds and policies;

paragraphs: This Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and related Notes and other financial information appearing elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, and with Part II, Item 7 ("Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations") of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended February 1, 2025, filed with the SEC on March 26, 2025, which provides a discussion of our financial condition and results of operations for Fiscal 2025 compared to our Fiscal 2024.
• Net sales increased 4.8% to $2.4 billion in Fiscal 2026 compared to Fiscal 2025.

• Journeys Group sales increased 7% and Schuh Group sales increased 4%, partially offset by a sales decrease of 4% at Genesco Brands Group, while Johnston & Murphy Group sales were flat for Fiscal 2026 as compared to Fiscal 2025.
• Total comparable sales increased 6% for Fiscal 2026, including a 6% increase in same store sales and a 4% increase in comparable e-commerce sales.
• Gross margin decreased 90 basis points as a percentage of net sales from 47.2% in Fiscal 2025 to 46.3% in Fiscal 2026.
• Selling and administrative expenses decreased 120 basis points as a percentage of net sales from 46.4% in Fiscal 2025 to 45.2% in Fiscal 2026.
• Operating margin increased 10 basis points as a percentage of net sales from 0.6% in Fiscal 2025 to 0.7% in Fiscal 2026.

• The effective income tax rate decreased from 309.6% in Fiscal 2025 to (5.4)% in Fiscal 2026 as a result of the impact of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ("OBBBA") in Fiscal 2026 and a $26.2 million valuation allowance in Fiscal 2025.
• Diluted earnings per share from continuing operations was $1.25 per share in Fiscal 2026 compared to a diluted loss per share from continuing operations of $1.80 per share in Fiscal 2025.

In assessing the performance of our business, we consider a variety of performance and financial measures. The key performance indicators we use to evaluate the financial condition and operating performance of our business are comparable sales, net sales, gross margin, operating income and operating margin. These key performance indicators should not be considered superior to, as a substitute for or as an alternative to, and should be considered in conjunction with, the U.S. GAAP financial measures presented herein. These measures may not be comparable to similarly-titled performance indicators used by other companies.

We consider comparable sales to be an important indicator of our current performance, and investors may find it useful as such. Comparable sales results are important to achieve leveraging of our costs, including occupancy, selling salaries, depreciation, etc. Comparable sales also have a direct impact on our total net revenue, working capital and cash. We define "comparable sales" as sales from stores open longer than one year, beginning with the first day a store has comparable sales (which we refer to in

this report as "same store sales"), and sales from websites operated longer than one year and direct mail catalog sales (which we refer to in this report as "comparable e-commerce sales"). Temporarily closed stores are excluded from the comparable sales calculation if closed for more than seven days. Expanded stores are excluded from the comparable sales calculation until the first day an expanded store has comparable prior year sales. Current year foreign exchange rates are applied to both current year and prior year comparable sales to achieve a consistent basis for comparison.

Our net sales for Fiscal 2026 increased 4.8% to $2.4 billion compared to $2.3 billion in Fiscal 2025. The net sales increase for Fiscal 2026 reflected a 6% increase in comparable sales, including a 6% increase in same store sales and a 4% increase in e-commerce comparable sales, and a favorable foreign exchange impact, partially offset by 42 net store closings and decreased wholesale sales. The consumer environment remains selective and intentional. Consumers tend to engage during key shopping moments and reduce discretionary spending outside of key shopping moments. Journeys Group had a strong year with comparable sales up 9%, fueled by strength in product assortment and other initiatives. Schuh Group comparable sales were flat for the year, reflecting the challenging retail environment in the U.K. Johnston & Murphy Group comparable sales were flat for the year reflecting lower store sales. Journeys Group sales increased 7% and Schuh Group sales increased 4%, partially offset by a sales decrease of 4% at Genesco Brands Group, reflecting the wind-down of Levis and other licenses, while Johnston & Murphy Group sales were flat for Fiscal 2026 compared to Fiscal 2025. Schuh Group's sales were flat on a local currency basis for Fiscal 2026.

Gross margin increased 2.7% to $1.127 billion in Fiscal 2026 from $1.097 billion in Fiscal 2025. Gross margin decreased 90 basis points as a percentage of net sales from 47.2% in Fiscal 2025 to 46.3% in Fiscal 2026, reflecting decreased gross margin as a percentage of net sales in Schuh Group and Genesco Brands Group, while gross margin as a percentage of net sales was flat in both Journeys Group and Johnston & Murphy Group. The overall decrease in gross margin as a percentage of net sales reflects increased promotional activity at Schuh Group and lower margins at Genesco Brands Group related to the exit of licenses and ongoing tariff pressure.

paragraphs: Genesco Inc., 1934 年於田納西州成立，為一家領先的鞋類、服飾及配件零售商與經銷商，其 Fiscal 2026 年淨銷售額為 2.4 十億美元。在 Fiscal 2026 年期間，我們運作四個應報告分部（不包括公司本部）：(i) Journeys Group，包含 Journeys®、Journeys Kidz® 及 Little Burgundy® 零售鞋類連鎖店與電商業務；(ii) Schuh Group，包含 Schuh 零售鞋類連鎖店與電商業務；(iii) Johnston & Murphy Group，包含 Johnston & Murphy® 零售業務、電商業務與 Johnston & Murphy® 品牌產品的經銷業務；以及 (iv) Genesco Brands Group，包含授權的 Dockers® ("Dockers") 及 Levi's® ("Levi's") 品牌，以及我們授權的其他鞋類品牌。我們也從事鞋類、服飾及配件的採購、設計、市場推廣與經銷業務，主要以 Johnston & Murphy 品牌、授權的 Dockers® 品牌、授權的 Levi's® 品牌及其他授權的鞋類品牌，向美國超過 900 家零售客戶銷售，包括多家領導的百貨公司、折扣店與專業商店，以及電商零售商。我們與 Levi's 的授權協議於 2026 年 5 月到期，我們正在退出該業務。
在 Fiscal 2026 年第二季，我們與 Kontoor Brands, Inc. ("Kontoor") 簽訂了一項多年授權協議，設計、採購、市場推廣並經銷男裝、女裝及童裝鞋類產品，使用 Wrangler® 品牌 ("Wrangler")。我們預期在 2026 年歷年秋季，根據該授權協議推出第一個 Wrangler 鞋類產品系列。

在 Fiscal 2026 年第三季，我們宣佈成立 Journeys Global Retail Group，將 Journeys、Schuh 及 Little Burgundy 統合。此一整合為我們的零售品牌創造了強大的機會，將業務定位為全球領先的時尚導向、年輕人鞋類零售集團，並專注於女性消費者。Journeys Global Retail Group 將提升我們的全球聲量，為品牌合作夥伴創造更大的成長潛力，並提升我們的頂級人才。
於 2026 年 1 月 31 日，我們經營 1,236 家零售鞋類、服飾及配件商店，主要位於美國與波多黎各，包括 63 家鞋類商店在加拿大，以及 118 家鞋類商店在英國 ("U.K.") 及愛爾蘭共和國 ("ROI")。我們預計在 Fiscal 2027 年開設約 23 家新零售商店，並關閉約 75 家零售商店，作為我們持續進行的商店優化努力的一部分。

財務年度的簡稱（例如 "Fiscal 2026"）指的是在命名年度最接近 1 月 31 日的星期六結尾的財務年度（例如 2026 年 1 月 31 日）。Fiscal 2026 年與 2025 年為 52 週年度，Fiscal 2024 年為 53 週年度。本文中所使用的 "公司"、"Genesco"、"我們"、"我們的" 或 "我們" 一詞，除非另有說明或根據上下文，均指 Genesco Inc. 及其子公司。本文所提及的 Item 7，"管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析" 的所有資訊，均於本報告的 Item 1 中引用，並於 Item 1 中引用。

本公司致力於創造與策劃具領導地位的鞋類品牌，這些品牌代表時尚、創新與自我表達，並成為消費者最喜愛的時尚鞋類購物目的地。每一家公司業務皆擁有強大的戰略地位，基於對所服務客羣深層且不斷進化的理解。我們努力與目標客羣建立長久的關係，運用對消費者與市場的深入洞察。我們力求激發並持續超越消費者期望，透過獨特的產品與體驗，運用我們在實體與數位通路的直接對消費者專業知識。我們的概念強度與長期建立的優勢，已確立了長久的領導地位，使我們的鞋類業務在各自領域表現卓越，但透過協同效應的益處，使它們變得更強大。我們已調整戰略，更加聚焦於消費者，以鞋類為核心的戰略，包含四大戰略成長驅動力：1) 創造與策劃成功產品，2) 提升我們獨特的零售與消費者品牌，3) 提供卓越的消費者體驗，4) 建立出色的團隊。我們預期未來會持續優化門店規模，專注於我們認為最具生產力的據點，同時關閉部分門店，但提升現有據點的生產力，並投資於門店翻新、技術與基礎設施，以支持全通路零售。
我們已進行過收購，包括2011年6月收購Schuh Group、2015年12月收購Little Burgundy以及2020年1月收購Togast。我們預期會專注於利用我們的直接對消費者能力，來成長我們的品牌平台，並在適當的時間運用其策略。

更廣泛而言，我們努力發展策略以緩解我們認為重要的風險，包括在上文「展望性陳述」中討論的風險，以及在項目1A「風險因素」中討論的風險。其中最重要的因素之一與消費者需求有關。經濟狀況可能影響需求，導致銷售變化，並因價格調整以促進銷售與管理存貨，進而影響毛利率。由於影響我們目標客羣的時尚趨勢可能快速變化，我們認為我們能迅速反應這些變化對我們的成功至關重要。即使我們成功地將商品選項與消費者偏好對齊，這些偏好仍可能影響結果，例如，推動銷售平均售價較低的產品，或更廣泛市場可取得的產品，因此較我們通常提供的產品更容易受到競爭壓力影響。此外，經濟因素，如通貨膨脹、供應鏈中斷與物流成本增加，以及任何未來的經濟衰退、通貨膨脹趨勢與稅收與關稅政策的變化，可能減少消費者的可支配所得或購買非必需品的意願，進而減少我們商品的需求，無論我們在偵測與回應時尚趨勢方面的技能如何。
Journeys Group在財務年度2026年佔本公司淨銷售額的61%。Journeys門店透過年輕化趨勢與多通路媒體，針對13至22歲的客羣。Journeys門店主要銷售價格範圍廣泛的品牌商品。Journeys Kidz門店主要銷售給年齡為嬰兒至12歲的年輕兒童的鞋類與配件。Little Burgundy門店銷售鞋類與配件給21至34歲的時尚導向男性與女性，從學生到年輕專業人士。
於2026年1月31日，Journeys Group營運965間門店，包括741間Journeys門店、194間Journeys Kidz門店與30間Little Burgundy門店，平均約2,100平方英呎，主要位於美國、波多黎各與加拿大各地的購物中心與工廠折扣中心，銷售給兒童、青少年與年輕成年人的鞋類與配件。Journeys
Group的電商網站包括以下：journeys.com、journeyskidz.com、journeys.ca與littleburgundyshoes.com。在財務年度2026年，Journeys Group關閉了41間門店（淨數）。

paragraphs: 本公司管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析應與本公司合併財務報表及其相關附註，以及其他財務資訊一併閱讀，這些資訊出現在本年度10-K申報表中，並與本公司年度10-K申報表中第二部分，第7項（"管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析"）之內容一併閱讀，該部分提供本公司財務狀況及營運成果於財務年度2025年與財務年度2024年之比較說明，該年度財務年度於2月1日結束，並於2025年3月26日提交至美國證券交易委員會。
• 淨銷售額成長 4.8% 至 2.4 十億美元，較財務年度 2025 年度成長。
• Journeys Group銷售額成長7%，Schuh Group銷售額成長4%，但Genesco Brands Group銷售額減少4%，此部分抵銷了成長幅度，而Johnston & Murphy Group銷售額在財務年度2026年與財務年度2025年相比維持不變。
• 總計可比銷售額於財務年度 2026 年成長 6%，包含同店銷售額成長 6% 與可比電商銷售額成長 4%。
• 毛利率以淨銷售額百分比計算，較財務年度2025年的47.2%下降90個基點，至財務年度2026年的46.3%。
• 銷售及行政費用以淨銷售額百分比計算，較財務年度2025年的46.4%下降120個基點，至財務年度2026年的45.2%。
• 營運毛利率以淨銷售額百分比計算，較財務年度2025年的0.6%成長10個基點，至財務年度2026年的0.7%。
• 實際所得稅率由財務年度2025年的309.6%下降至財務年度2026年的(5.4)%，係因財務年度2026年受One Big Beautiful Bill Act（"OBBBA"）之影響，以及財務年度2025年有26.2百萬美元之價值減損準備所致。
• 連續營運之稀釋每股盈餘為 2026 財年每股 1.25 美元，與 2025 財年連續營運之稀釋每股虧損每股 1.80 美元相比。
在評估我們業務表現時，我們考量多種績效與財務指標。我們用以評估本公司財務狀況與營運表現的關鍵績效指標為可比銷售額、淨銷售額、毛利率、營運收入與營運毛利率。這些關鍵績效指標不應被視為優於、取代或作為 U.S. GAAP 財務指標的替代方案，而應與 herein 所列示的 U.S. GAAP 財務指標一併考量。這些指標可能與其他公司使用之相同名稱的績效指標不具可比性。
我們認為可比銷售額是衡量我們當前表現的重要指標，投資人也可能認為此指標具有參考價值。可比銷售額結果對實現我們的成本槓桿作用至關重要，包括租金、銷售薪資、折舊等。可比銷售額也對我們總淨收入、營運資本與現金有直接影響。我們將「可比銷售額」定義為營業超過一年的商店銷售額，從商店開始有可比銷售額的第一天（我們稱為
本報告中所稱之「同店銷售」，係指營運逾一年之網站銷售及直郵目錄銷售（我們在本報告中稱之為「可比電商銷售」）。若商店關閉逾七日，則關閉之商店將不計入可比銷售計算。擴張後之商店，則在擴張後商店首次出現與前一年可比銷售數據之前，將不計入可比銷售計算。本年度之外匯匯率已應用於本年度及前一年度之可比銷售，以達到一致之比較基礎。

本公司財務年度2026之淨銷售額較財務年度2025之23億美元增加4.8%至24億美元。財務年度2026之淨銷售額增加，反映可比銷售增加6%，包括同店銷售增加6%及電商可比銷售增加4%，加上有利之外匯影響，部分抵銷42家商店關閉及整體批發銷售減少。消費環境持續保持選擇性與有意圖性。消費者傾向於在重要購物時刻參與活動，並在非重要購物時刻減少非必要開支。Journeys Group 本年度可比銷售成長9%，因產品種類多元化及其他計畫表現強勁。Schuh Group 本年度可比銷售持平，反映英國零售環境困難。Johnston & Murphy Group 本年度可比銷售持平，反映商店銷售減少。Journeys Group 銷售成長7%，Schuh Group 銷售成長4%，部分抵銷Genesco Brands Group 銷售減少4%，反映Levis及其他授權品牌退出營運，而Johnston & Murphy Group 本年度財務年度2026銷售與財務年度2025持平。Schuh Group 本年度財務年度2026銷售以本幣計算為持平。

毛利率在財務年度2026增加2.7%至11.27億美元，較財務年度2025之10.97億美元。毛利率以淨銷售額百分比計算，從財務年度2025之47.2%降至財務年度2026之46.3%，減少90個基點，反映Schuh Group 及Genesco Brands Group 之毛利率以淨銷售額百分比計算下降，而Journeys Group 及Johnston & Murphy Group 之毛利率以淨銷售額百分比計算維持不變。整體毛利率以淨銷售額百分比計算下降，反映Schuh Group 增加促銷活動，以及Genesco Brands Group 因退出授權及持續關稅壓力導致邊際率下降。

headings: 競爭、需求相關及聲譽風險
消費者支出受不佳及/或波動的經濟條件及其他因素影響，可能顯著損害我們的業務，影響我們的財務狀況、流動性及營運成果。
未能保護我們的聲譽，可能對我們的品牌名稱產生重大不利影響。
我們的成功取決於我們應對變動的消費者偏好、識別及解讀消費者趨勢，並成功行銷新產品的能力。
我們未能適當處理 emerging sustainability 事項，可能對我們的聲譽產生重大不利影響，進而影響我們的業務。
我們的結果可能因購物中心消費者人潮下降而受到不利影響。
我們的營運成果受季節性及季度性波動影響。
零售業的變化可能對我們的業務或財務狀況產生重大不利影響。
本公司業務屬高度競爭性，增加或新興競爭者可能對本公司造成重大不利影響。
若本公司或客戶的線上電商網站無法有效運作或未能符合客戶的期待或偏好，將可能對本公司業務及財務結果造成重大不利影響。
投資與基礎建設風險
本公司在開設新門店及續約現有門店租約時，面臨多項風險。
本公司所進行的併購或新業務啟動，以及資產或業務的處分，均涉及一定程度的風險。
因併購而記入的商譽，可能因減值而影響本公司利潤。
科技、資料安全與隱私權風險
本公司業務的運作高度依賴資訊系統。
本公司資訊科技重整計畫可能無法達成預期成果，並可能幹擾本公司營運作業。
本公司面臨與付款相關的風險，這些風險可能增加本公司營運成本、使本公司面臨詐欺或竊盜的風險、使本公司承擔潛在責任，並幹擾本公司營運。
若發生資料外洩，無論是透過網路安全事件或其他方式，或未能遵守資料保護法規，可能對本公司營運造成重大不利影響。
資料保護要求持續演進，這些要求可能對本公司營運及營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司在營運中對機械學習及其他類型人工智慧的應用、擴展與管理，可能對本公司營運、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
營運、供應鏈及第三方風險
營運成本增加，包括因最低工資潛在提高或競爭壓力導致的工資增加，可能對本公司營運成果造成不利影響。
若本公司失去關鍵管理層或無法吸引並留住營運所需人才，本公司營運成果可能受損。
我們其中一個配送中心遺失或發生中斷，以及影響商品分銷的其他因素，包括運輸費用，可能會對我們的業務造成重大不利影響。
我們進口產品的成本增加或進口產品流通中斷，可能會對我們的業務造成不利影響。
我們銷售的商品依賴第三方供應商及授權方。
稅務、法律、法規、全球及其他外部風險
稅法的變更可能導致我們的有效稅率出現較大的波動。
建立並保護我們的智慧財產權對我們的業務至關重要。
我們非美國業務的範圍使我們的表現面臨風險，包括外國、政治、法律及經濟條件以及匯率波動。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨多種風險，這些風險可能對本公司業務產生重大影響。請您謹慎考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，以及本年度10-K形式年度報告中其他資訊，包括本公司合併財務報表與該報表的附註。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。此外，我們目前未知或認為不重要的其他風險與不確定性，也可能影響本公司業務運作與財務表現。若下列所描述的任何事件發生，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、現金流或營運成果產生重大負面影響。這可能會導致本公司股票交易價格下跌，甚至大幅下跌，您可能損失部分或全部投資。
本公司業務的成功在很大程度上取決於總體消費支出水平以及本公司產品類別。影響我們所提供商品總體消費支出水平的因素可能包括，但不限於：
• 總體經濟與產業條件，包括與經濟衰退或其他總體經濟條件及壓力相關的風險，例如通貨膨脹影響與供應鏈挑戰；
• 天氣條件；• 能源成本，影響汽油與住宅加熱價格；• 消費者負債水平；
• 產品價格，包括課徵關稅的影響；• 利率；
• 公共衛生問題（包括疫情與隔離措施）；• 稅率、稅款退還與稅務政策；
